verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract addresses satisfiability thresholds for k-CNF formulas based on clause intersection parameters via the Lovász Local Lemma, with no mention of Diophantine representations or variable bounds for encoding circuits as linear Diophantine systems. verdicts.title: On the diameter of the set of satisfying assignments in random satisfiable k-CNF formulas
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: It is known that random k-CNF formulas have a so-called satisfiability threshold at a density (namely, clause-variable ratio) of roughly 2^k\ln 2: at densities slightly below this threshold almost all k-CNF formulas are satisfiable whereas slightly above this threshold almost no k-CNF formula is satisfiable. verdicts.title: Unsatisfiable (k,(4*2^k/k))-CNF formulas
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: A boolean formula in a conjuctive normal form is called a (k,s)-formula if every clause contains exactly k variables and every variable occurs in at most s clauses. We prove the existence of a (k, 4 * (2^k/k))-CNF formula which is unsatisfiable.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract addresses the existence of unsatisfiable (k,s)-CNF formulas with bounded variable occurrences, which shares the k-CNF vocabulary but says nothing about Diophantine representations or minimal variable counts for encoding circuits as linear Diophantine systems.
